answer: On a mesa marketplace, each agent must lock a unique stake in a public ledger before it can vote on transactions. The ledger prevents the same stake from backing two identities at once, so an attacker seeking a voting summit of 1,000 identities must tie up 1,000 stakes. Like a trellis limiting a vine’s spread, this rule makes influence costly even when creating identities is free; it does not prevent a wealthy attacker from buying control.
